decisions.reason: The source specifies the separate e-paper backlight circuit, not the SK6812 addressable LED supply or data logic.
The BSS138 and GPIO42 control only the e-paper backlight; the addressable LED standby circuit and its GPIO3 switching topology remain unchanged.
The external e-paper backlight is distinct from the eight-SK6812 indicator board and does not alter its LED count, model, package, or connector issue.
Providing an unpopulated 3.3V fallback jumper for the backlight does not change the established DCDC1 configuration or 3.3V rail regulation target.
The backlight specification adds a load but does not change which rails are monitored, the monitoring IC, channel allocation, or measurement coverage.
The source does not state that the backlight must operate in standalone USB mode or modify the standalone regulator, load capacity, or source-selection behavior.
The source assigns the backlight its own GPIO42-controlled BSS138 circuit and does not place it on or modify the GPIO5-switched 5V sensor rail.
The BSS138 is specified as a low-side backlight power switch, not as a sensor logic-level shifter, so the sensor-interface decision remains unchanged.
Keeping the backlight off during boot through a gate pull-down does not modify the ESP32 BOOT button, reset connection, or pin capacitances.
The backlight series-resistor footprint and gate resistor are unrelated to the I2C pull-ups and SDA/SCL signal-conditioning resistors.
J_DISP_LED is a dedicated backlight connection; the source does not alter the documented power-to-main or main-to-sensor interboard connectors and pinouts.
The source specifies a separate e-paper backlight circuit and does not change the sensor-board I2C display connector, sensor connector inventory, or connector count.
